newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The cabinet has approved all of the proposals made by the Forum of the Poor - in principle. The forum says it welcomes the move - in principle - but will not call off its rally until action replaced words. Top of the demands are the government's agreement to end relocations and to set up a committee to prove villagers' land ownership claims. The demands focus on cases of 107 upland villages in the North. (BANGKOK POST)

- After heavy criticism by Democrat members of Parliament and the media, Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung has made an abrupt about-turn, saying his sons may have been involved in a brawl in a bar in Phuket province last weekend. The outspoken minister says while his sons have told him they have nothing to do with the fight, they may not have told him the facts. (THE NATION)

- Deputy Science, Technology and Environment Minister Adisorn Piengket has reiterated the October 14 memorial project will definitely be realised despite protest in some quarters. The deputy minister claims that only a handful of people, including some "big" officials, are against the project "which is quite normal". (BANGKOK POST)

- Surasak Nanakul, economic adviser to the prime minister, says the Bank of Thailand (BOT) should urgently transfer funds from the banking sector to cash-strapped finance companies, starting with 20 billion baht in the Government Pension Fund. The finance sector's liquidity crisis-deepened over the past two months as depositors withdrew funds from finance companies and transferred their deposits to banks. As a result, the banking sector is experiencing excess liquidity, while the finance sector faces a severe shortage of funds. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan has hinted at three long-term measures to reform government budget allocations by proposing amendments to the expenditure budget law. In the meantime, the Chavalit government will try to reduce the commitment budgets for fiscal 1998 by transferring funds from construction schemes where land expropriation has not been completed, to new projects. (THE NATION) (BUSINESS DAY) - Thailand is looking seriously at Burma for additional gas supplies, despite political controversy fuelled by the Yadana and Yetagun deals. The Petroleum Authority of Thailand is focusing on gas-prospective blocks operated by the U.S. company Atlantic Richfield in Burma's Gulf of Martaban as an additional source of foreign natural gas supplies. (BANGKOK POST)
